bull_bear.body:
- Established licensing arrangements giving access to several internationally recognised brands (Disney, Nickelodeon, Barbie, Marvel, Minions, Paw Patrol), enhancing product appeal and consumer recall
- Portfolio of proprietary IPs (Pugs at Play, Gurliez, Fanster, Beezy Kits, Minds at Play, SHDZ, Boujee) that supports brand building and margin improvement
- Integrated end-to-end model from concept creation and design through sourcing and third-party manufacture to distribution, positioning it as a preferred partner for licensed merchandise and custom-developed toys
- Asset-light and scalable business model that supports growth while maintaining operational flexibility
- International distribution reach through wholly owned Middle East subsidiaries supported by distributors and direct partnerships
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on third-party licensing arrangements — Reliance on licensing arrangements with third-party brand owners carries risks around renewal, cost structures and continuity of key product lines, and the Company depends on them for certain product segments.
- Rapidly changing consumer preferences and short product life cycles — Shorter product life cycles require continuous innovation and efficient inventory management; an inability to adapt may impact sales and margins.
- Input cost, logistics and foreign-exchange volatility — The business is subject to fluctuations in raw material prices, logistics costs and foreign exchange rates, particularly given its international operations and Middle East presence through subsidiaries.
- Geopolitical exposure to the Middle East — Regional conflicts and geopolitical developments disrupted trade routes, supply chain networks, logistics operations and consumer sentiment, indirectly affecting demand patterns, order execution timelines and market conditions in a region where the Company operates through subsidiaries.
- Stringent regulatory and product-safety standards across jurisdictions — Compliance with safety and regulatory standards in domestic and international markets may increase compliance requirements and timelines.
- Intense competition — The Company faces intense competition from domestic as well as international players in a competitive and dynamic industry.
- Global economic uncertainty and supply-chain disruption — Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions may affect both demand and sourcing.
- Internal control framework still being built out — Internal controls rely on internal audits by an independent firm of Chartered Accountants and Audit Committee review, while ERP implementation is still under process and its completion is expected to further enhance the financial control framework.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company is engaged in licensing, own-brand development and distribution of toys and children's consumer merchandise, offering end-to-end solutions spanning product design and development, sourcing and distribution to leading retail formats across India and select international markets. It caters to children between 18 months and 15 years of age, combining licensed products from internationally recognised brands with a portfolio of proprietary intellectual properties, and manufactures through third-party partners rather than owning production. Its integrated model runs the full value chain from concept creation and product design to sourcing, third-party manufacture and distribution, with a Middle East presence built through wholly owned subsidiaries.

business.body:

- Portfolio of proprietary IPs (Pugs at Play, Gurliez, Fanster, Beezy Kits, Minds at Play, SHDZ, Boujee) that supports brand building and margin improvement
- Integrated end-to-end model from concept creation and design through sourcing and third-party manufacture to distribution, positioning it as a preferred partner for licensed merchandise and custom-developed toys

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Deepen the Middle East presence through the wholly owned subsidiaries, expanding the distribution network and strengthening relationships with key retail and channel partners
- Expand the portfolio of proprietary intellectual properties alongside strategic licensing partnerships to enhance brand visibility, improve margins and diversify the product portfolio
- Expand into high-potential segments such as figurines and collectibles, and develop consumer-centric products around emerging consumer trends
- Optimise the supply chain and leverage global sourcing opportunities while strengthening omni-channel distribution capabilities
- Retain the asset-light, scalable business model to support efficient growth and operational flexibility
- Progressively develop own IPs in branded toys and consumer products to improve competitive positioning against global industry participants
- Continue the integrated end-to-end model spanning concept creation, design, sourcing, third-party manufacture and distribution to remain a preferred partner for licensed merchandise
- The Company reports no associates or joint ventures and states that it has neither granted loans nor provided guarantees under Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013 during FY2025-26; the only Section 186 activity disclosed is an equity investment taking 100% of Striders FZ LLC. Related-party contracts are stated to be in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis, and were not material enough to require Form AOC-2. A Risk Management Policy and a CSR Policy are in place, with CSR responsibilities discharged by the Board itself as a CSR Committee is not mandatory. No dividend or payout philosophy is stated in the sections supplied.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company describes itself as asset-light and scalable, manufacturing through third-party partners, so expansion is footprint- and channel-led rather than plant-led; no capacity addition, commissioning or capital-expenditure project is described in this bundle. Expansion during FY2025-26 was corporate and geographic: the Company converted from a private limited to a public limited company (members' approval at the EGM held on July 18, 2025) and completed an IPO of 50,40,000 fresh Equity Shares together with an Offer for Sale of 5,08,800 Equity Shares, receiving NSE in-principle approval on February 10, 2026 and final listing and trading approval on March 05, 2026, with trading on the NSE EMERGE (SME) Platform commencing March 06, 2026. On the operating footprint, Striders Hub General Trading LLC, Dubai, UAE was incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary during the year, adding to the existing wholly owned subsidiaries Striders FZ LLC, UAE and Striders Distribution & Services Private Limited, India. Forward expansion intent stated in the outlook is to deepen the Middle East regional presence and expand the distribution network, expand the proprietary IP portfolio alongside licensing partnerships, move into high-potential segments such as figurines and collectibles, optimise the supply chain and global sourcing, and strengthen omni-channel distribution. The Board deferred any dividend for FY2025-26 expressly to conserve resources for future expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing demand for licensed and branded toys, driven by digital content and character-based engagement
- Expansion of organised retail formats and continued penetration of e-commerce platforms, enhancing market reach and visibility
- Increasing consumer spending on globally recognised brands and growing brand awareness among younger demographics
- Increasing preference for kid-adult toys and collectibles
- India emerging as a key sourcing and manufacturing hub under global supply chain diversification strategies
- Middle East subsidiaries enabling deeper market penetration and revenue diversification
- Proprietary IP development positioned as a lever for brand building and margin improvement
- Near-term headwind: geopolitical developments and regional conflicts in the Middle East disrupted trade routes, supply chains, logistics and consumer sentiment, indirectly affecting demand patterns and order execution timelines
- Cost pressures, evolving regulatory requirements and changing consumer preferences are expected to persist

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company describes itself as asset-light and scalable, manufacturing through third-party partners, so expansion is footprint- and channel-led rather than plant-led; no capacity addition, commissioning or capital-expenditure project is described in this bundle. Expansion during FY2025-26 was corporate and geographic: the Company converted from a private limited to a public limited company (members' approval at the EGM held on July 18, 2025) and completed an IPO of 50,40,000 fresh Equity Shares together with an Offer for Sale of 5,08,800 Equity Shares, receiving NSE in-principle approval on February 10, 2026 and final listing and trading approval on March 05, 2026, with trading on the NSE EMERGE (SME) Platform commencing March 06, 2026. On the operating footprint, Striders Hub General Trading LLC, Dubai, UAE was incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary during the year, adding to the existing wholly owned subsidiaries Striders FZ LLC, UAE and Striders Distribution & Services Private Limited, India. Forward expansion intent stated in the outlook is to deepen the Middle East regional presence and expand the distribution network, expand the proprietary IP portfolio alongside licensing partnerships, move into high-potential segments such as figurines and collectibles, optimise the supply chain and global sourcing, and strengthen omni-channel distribution. The Board deferred any dividend for FY2025-26 expressly to conserve resources for future expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established licensing arrangements giving access to several internationally recognised brands (Disney, Nickelodeon, Barbie, Marvel, Minions, Paw Patrol), enhancing product appeal and consumer recall
- Portfolio of proprietary IPs (Pugs at Play, Gurliez, Fanster, Beezy Kits, Minds at Play, SHDZ, Boujee) that supports brand building and margin improvement
- Integrated end-to-end model from concept creation and design through sourcing and third-party manufacture to distribution, positioning it as a preferred partner for licensed merchandise and custom-developed toys
- Asset-light and scalable business model that supports growth while maintaining operational flexibility
- International distribution reach through wholly owned Middle East subsidiaries supported by distributors and direct partnerships

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on third-party licensing arrangements — Reliance on licensing arrangements with third-party brand owners carries risks around renewal, cost structures and continuity of key product lines, and the Company depends on them for certain product segments.
- Rapidly changing consumer preferences and short product life cycles — Shorter product life cycles require continuous innovation and efficient inventory management; an inability to adapt may impact sales and margins.
- Input cost, logistics and foreign-exchange volatility — The business is subject to fluctuations in raw material prices, logistics costs and foreign exchange rates, particularly given its international operations and Middle East presence through subsidiaries.
- Geopolitical exposure to the Middle East — Regional conflicts and geopolitical developments disrupted trade routes, supply chain networks, logistics operations and consumer sentiment, indirectly affecting demand patterns, order execution timelines and market conditions in a region where the Company operates through subsidiaries.
- Stringent regulatory and product-safety standards across jurisdictions — Compliance with safety and regulatory standards in domestic and international markets may increase compliance requirements and timelines.
- Intense competition — The Company faces intense competition from domestic as well as international players in a competitive and dynamic industry.
- Global economic uncertainty and supply-chain disruption — Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions may affect both demand and sourcing.
- Internal control framework still being built out — Internal controls rely on internal audits by an independent firm of Chartered Accountants and Audit Committee review, while ERP implementation is still under process and its completion is expected to further enhance the financial control framework.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen the Middle East presence through the wholly owned subsidiaries, expanding the distribution network and strengthening relationships with key retail and channel partners
- Expand the portfolio of proprietary intellectual properties alongside strategic licensing partnerships to enhance brand visibility, improve margins and diversify the product portfolio
